newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid prices gain with crude.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid prices gain with crude.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices moved higher again Friday in thin, late trade, boosted by another sharp rally in crude despite fading East Coast generation demand, industry sources said.

"There's a stronger underlying tone in the market. And another big move in crude certainly helped, but there's not a lot of demand and next week demand should really dry up," said one East Coast trader, adding Gulf Coast barrels were a little tight.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent firmed a quarter to about $16.25 a barrel, traders said.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour inched up slightly to about $16.75.
New York high sulphurs also scored gains, with 2.2 percent firming a quarter to about $15.
At the U.S. Gulf, three percent jumped 50 cents to $15, while one percent was 35 cents higher at $15.25.
A Florida utility awarded 90,000 barrels of three percent for delivery by June 15 at $15.70 (delivered).

New York city gate weekend gas prices slipped five cents Friday to the low-$2.40s/mmBtu, or about $15.25 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, fell a similar amount to about $2.18/mmBtu, or $13.73 a barrel.
Traders noted that gas this week regained the competitive edge over fuel for prompt or forward supplies.
